title: Values, references & parameter passing
learningObjectives: Only the reference value was copied; the parameter is a separate local variable.
Explain the mechanism using the runnable example.

explanationMd:
## The central idea

A Java variable always holds a value. For a primitive, that value is the primitive itself. For an object variable, it is a reference value. Method invocation copies that value into a new parameter variable. Reassigning the parameter cannot reassign the caller's variable. Mutating the shared object can still be observed through both references. These are separate operations, which is why describing Java as passing objects by reference causes confusion.

## Follow the mechanism

The heap object and the local reference occupy different conceptual roles. A method can receive a copied address-like reference, follow it and modify a field, yet replacing its parameter only changes the local copy. Do not depend on an actual memory-address representation: the JVM is free to move objects during collection. Alias reasoning is the useful model. Two variables may refer to the same mutable object, and that shared identity makes mutation visible.

Compile it as `Main.java` with Java 21 or later, then run `java Main`. An observed output is evidence about this execution; the explanation must still follow the language or library contract rather than an accidental implementation detail. ## Move from a demonstration to a service

The mutation changes the original array object, while the later reassignment directs only the local parameter toward a new array. The caller keeps its original reference. Identity asks whether two references designate the same object. Logical equality asks whether they represent the same value. Collection choice starts with workload, ordering and identity requirements. ArrayList provides indexed access and amortized constant-time append, but inserting at the front shifts existing elements. ## The central idea

Dependency injection means supplying an object's collaborators from outside rather than constructing them inside business methods. A Spring container automates construction and lifecycle management, but it does not change the dependency graph's design responsibilities. Circular dependencies often reveal mixed responsibilities. Keep request-specific data in method parameters or appropriately scoped objects.

## The central idea

Deadlock occurs when participants wait on a cycle of resources that none can release while waiting. If one operation locks account A then B and another locks B then A, each may hold one monitor while waiting for the other. Timeouts can make waits bounded, but the caller still needs to unwind partial work and report failure without violating the business invariant.
